# Tour of forward sensing operators

This example provides a tour of some of the forward operators implemented in DeepInverse.
We restrict ourselves to operators where the signal is a 2D image. The full list of operators can be found in
[here](https://deepinv.org/user_guide/physics/physics.html.md#physics).

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 10-17 -->
```Python
import torch

import deepinv as dinv
from deepinv.utils.plotting import plot
from deepinv.utils import load_example
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 18-22 -->

## Load image from the internet

This example uses an image of the CBSD68 dataset.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 22-33 -->
```Python
device = dinv.utils.get_device()

x = load_example("CBSD_0010.png", grayscale=False).to(device)

x = torch.tensor(x, device=device, dtype=torch.float)
x = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(x, size=(64, 64))
img_size = x.shape[1:]
# Set the global random seed from pytorch to ensure reproducibility of the example.
torch.manual_seed(0)
```

## Denoising

The denoising class [`deepinv.physics.Denoising`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Denoising.html.md#deepinv.physics.Denoising) is associated with an identity operator.
In this example we choose a Poisson noise.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 39-47 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.Denoising(dinv.physics.PoissonNoise(0.1))

y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot([x, y], titles=["signal", "measurement"])
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 48-54 -->

## Inpainting

The inpainting class [`deepinv.physics.Inpainting`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Inpainting.html.md#deepinv.physics.Inpainting) is associated with a mask operator.
The mask is generated at random (unless an explicit mask is provided as input).
We also consider Gaussian noise in this example.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 54-69 -->
```Python
sigma = 0.1  # noise level
physics = dinv.physics.Inpainting(
    mask=0.5,
    img_size=x.shape[1:],
    noise_model=dinv.physics.GaussianNoise(sigma=sigma),
    device=device,
)

y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot([x, y], titles=["signal", "measurement"])
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 70-75 -->

## Demosaicing

The demosaicing class [`deepinv.physics.Demosaicing`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Demosaicing.html.md#deepinv.physics.Demosaicing) is associated with a Bayer pattern,
which is a color filter array used in digital cameras (see [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayer_filter)).

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 75-83 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.Demosaicing(img_size=(64, 64), device=device)

y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot([x, y], titles=["signal", "measurement"])
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 84-89 -->

## Compressed Sensing

The compressed sensing class [`deepinv.physics.CompressedSensing`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.CompressedSensing.html.md#deepinv.physics.CompressedSensing) is associated with a random Gaussian matrix.
Here we take 2048 measurements of an image of size 64x64, which corresponds to a compression ratio of 2.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 89-102 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.CompressedSensing(
    m=2048,
    channelwise=True,
    img_size=img_size,
    device=device,
)

y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot([x, physics.A_dagger(y)], titles=["signal", "linear inverse"])
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 103-113 -->

## Computed Tomography

The class [`deepinv.physics.Tomography`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Tomography.html.md#deepinv.physics.Tomography) is associated with the sparse Radon transform.
Here we take 40 views of an image of size 64x64, and consider mixed Poisson-Gaussian noise.

#### NOTE
The filtered backprojection (FBP) can be computed using the method [`deepinv.physics.Tomography.fbp()`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Tomography.html.md#deepinv.physics.Tomography.fbp) of the physics object.
This does not coincide with the linear pseudo-inverse, computed with [`deepinv.physics.Tomography.A_dagger()`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Tomography.html.md#deepinv.physics.Tomography.A_dagger)

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 113-130 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.Tomography(
    img_width=img_size[-1],
    angles=40,
    device=device,
    noise_model=dinv.physics.PoissonGaussianNoise(gain=0.001, sigma=0.001),
    normalize=True,
)

y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot(
    [x, (y - y.min()) / y.max(), physics.fbp(y), physics.A_dagger(y)],
    titles=["signal", "sinogram", "filt. backproj.", "linear inverse"],
)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 131-141 -->

## MRI

The class [`deepinv.physics.MRI`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.MRI.html.md#deepinv.physics.MRI) is associated with a subsampling of the Fourier transform.
The mask indicates which Fourier coefficients are measured. Here we use a random Cartesian mask, which
corresponds to a compression ratio of approximately 4.

#### NOTE
The signal must be complex-valued for this operator, where the first channel corresponds to the real part
and the second channel to the imaginary part. In this example, we set the imaginary part to zero.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 141-161 -->
```Python
mask = torch.rand((1, img_size[-1]), device=device) > 0.75
mask = torch.ones((img_size[-2], 1), device=device) * mask
mask[:, int(img_size[-1] / 2) - 2 : int(img_size[-1] / 2) + 2] = 1

physics = dinv.physics.MRI(
    mask=mask, device=device, noise_model=dinv.physics.GaussianNoise(sigma=0.05)
)

x2 = torch.cat(
    [x[:, 0, :, :].unsqueeze(1), torch.zeros_like(x[:, 0, :, :].unsqueeze(1))], dim=1
)
y = physics(x2)

# plot results
plot(
    [x2, mask.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0), physics.A_adjoint(y)],
    titles=["signal", "k-space mask", "linear inverse"],
)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 162-164 -->

We also provide physics generators for various accelerated MRI masks.
These are Cartesian sampling strategies and can be used for static (k) and dynamic (k-t) undersampling:

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 165-186 -->
```Python
from deepinv.physics.generator import (
    GaussianMaskGenerator,
    RandomMaskGenerator,
    EquispacedMaskGenerator,
)

# shape (C, T, H, W)
mask_gaussian = GaussianMaskGenerator((2, 8, 64, 50), acceleration=4).step()["mask"]
mask_uniform = EquispacedMaskGenerator((2, 8, 64, 50), acceleration=4).step()["mask"]
mask_random = RandomMaskGenerator((2, 8, 64, 50), acceleration=4).step()["mask"]

plot(
    [
        mask_gaussian[:, :, 0, ...],
        mask_uniform[:, :, 0, ...],
        mask_random[:, :, 0, ...],
    ],
    titles=["Gaussian", "Uniform", "Random uniform"],
)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 187-192 -->

## Decolorize

The class [`deepinv.physics.Decolorize`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Decolorize.html.md#deepinv.physics.Decolorize) is associated with a simple
color-to-gray operator.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 192-200 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.Decolorize(device=device)

y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot([x, y], titles=["signal", "measurement"])
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 201-206 -->

## Pan-sharpening

The class [`deepinv.physics.Pansharpen`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Pansharpen.html.md#deepinv.physics.Pansharpen) obtains measurements which consist of
a high-resolution grayscale image and a low-resolution RGB image.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 206-214 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.Pansharpen(img_size=img_size, device=device)

y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot([x, y[0], y[1]], titles=["signal", "low res rgb", "high res gray"])
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 215-220 -->

## Single-Pixel Camera

The single-pixel camera class [`deepinv.physics.SinglePixelCamera`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.SinglePixelCamera.html.md#deepinv.physics.SinglePixelCamera) is associated with `m` binary patterns.
When `fast=True`, the patterns are generated using a fast Hadamard transform.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 220-231 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.SinglePixelCamera(
    m=1024, fast=True, ordering="cake_cutting", img_size=img_size, device=device
)

y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot([x, physics.A_adjoint(y)], titles=["signal", "linear inverse"])
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 232-237 -->

## Blur

The class [`deepinv.physics.Blur`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Blur.html.md#deepinv.physics.Blur) blurs the input image with a specified kernel.
Here we use a Gaussian blur with a standard deviation of 2 pixels and an angle of 45 degrees.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 237-248 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.Blur(
    dinv.physics.functional.gaussian_blur(sigma=(2, 0.1), angle=45.0), device=device
)

y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot([x, y], titles=["signal", "measurement"])
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 249-253 -->

## Super-Resolution

The downsampling class [`deepinv.physics.Downsampling`](https://deepinv.org/api/stubs/deepinv.physics.Downsampling.html.md#deepinv.physics.Downsampling) is associated with a downsampling operator.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 253-264 -->
```Python
physics = dinv.physics.Downsampling(
    img_size=img_size, factor=2, device=device, filter="bicubic"
)


y = physics(x)

# plot results
plot([x, y], titles=["signal", "measurement"])
```
